title: Executive Order 14409: Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security (91 FR 34565)

covered_actors: Executive departments and agencies (CNSS, Department of War, NSA, DHS/CISA, Treasury, OMB, OPM, Commerce/NIST, DOJ)
AI developers and researchers (including developers of covered frontier models)
Operators of critical infrastructure (including rural hospitals, community banks, and local utilities)
Criminal actors utilizing AI or AI agents for unauthorized computer access or fraud
prohibited_practices: Utilizing AI or employing AI agents to illegally access or damage a computer without authorization, breach any public or private IT system, unlawfully access data for criminal or unlawful purposes, or commit related identity theft or wire fraud under 18 U.S.C. 1028, 1030, and 1343

evidence.quote: develop and maintain a classified benchmarking process to assess the advanced cyber capabilities of AI models and determine the threshold at which an AI model should be designated a “covered frontier model” for the purposes of this order, sharing such assessments with AI developers and researchers as appropriate.

provide the Federal Government with access to covered frontier models, subject to appropriate confidentiality, cybersecurity, insider-risk, and intellectual-property protection, use, and nondisclosure requirements, for a period of up to 30 days before they plan to release such models to other trusted partners;

shall release Binding Operational Directives and other guidance as appropriate to:
(i) expedite and prioritize the cyber defense of civilian Federal Government information systems in order to protect our Nation's vital functions;

Within 30 days of the date of this order, the Committee on National Security Systems shall prioritize the cyber defense of National Security Systems, as defined in
44 U.S.C. 3552(b)(6)(A)
, by taking appropriate and expeditious action consistent with the purpose of this order.

The Attorney General shall prioritize the enforcement of
18 U.S.C. 1028
,
18 U.S.C. 1030
,
18 U.S.C. 1343
, and all other applicable Federal criminal laws against anyone who utilizes AI to illegally access or damage a computer without authorization, or who utilizes AI while engaged in such illegal access to further any other crime.

the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs, and the National Cyber Director, shall release Binding Operational Directives and other guidance as appropriate

Nothing in this section shall be construed to authorize the creation of a mandatory governmental licensing, preclearance, or permitting requirement for the development, publication, release, or distribution of new AI models, including frontier models.

shall form an AI cybersecurity clearinghouse, in voluntary collaboration with the AI industry and operators of critical infrastructure, that coordinates and deconflicts scanning for software vulnerabilities, discovers and validates such vulnerabilities, and coordinates and prioritizes remediation and distribution of vulnerability patches.

enforcement_authorities: Secretary of Homeland Security / Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
Secretary of War / National Security Agency (NSA)
Secretary of Commerce / National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
compliance_deadlines: Within 30 days of 2026-06-02 (2026-07-02): CNSS and Secretary of War to prioritize cyber defense of National Security Systems and Department of War information systems
Within 30 days of 2026-06-02 (2026-07-02): DHS/CISA to release Binding Operational Directives and guidance for civilian federal cyber defense, AI defensive tools, and critical-infrastructure access
Within 30 days of 2026-06-02 (2026-07-02): Treasury, NSA, CISA, and National Cyber Director to form voluntary AI cybersecurity clearinghouse for vulnerability scanning and patching
Within 30 days of 2026-06-02 (2026-07-02): OMB to determine whether Federal grant programs have available funding for advanced AI vulnerability detection
Within 60 days of 2026-06-02 (2026-08-01): OPM to expand U.S. Tech Force Information Cybersecurity Specialist hiring and placement pathways

Within 60 days of 2026-06-02 (2026-08-01): Treasury, NSA, CISA, National Cyber Director, APST, and NIST to develop classified frontier cyber benchmarking process and voluntary up-to-30-day pre-release federal access framework
policy_extraction.penalties_summary: Directs the Attorney General to prioritize federal criminal prosecution under 18 U.S.C. 1028 (identity fraud), 18 U.S.C. 1030 (Computer Fraud and Abuse Act), 18 U.S.C. 1343 (wire fraud), and other applicable federal criminal statutes against malicious actors using AI or AI agents for unauthorized computer access or data theft; explicitly prohibits construing Section 3 as authorizing mandatory government licensing, preclearance, or permitting for AI models.
policy_extraction.implementation_notes: Signed June 2, 2026 and published June 5, 2026 (91 FR 34565). Pairs mandatory federal agency cyber-defense hardening (via CNSS, Department of War, and CISA Binding Operational Directives) and prioritized DOJ criminal enforcement against malicious AI/agent cyber intrusions with voluntary private-sector collaboration—specifically an AI cybersecurity clearinghouse and an NSA-led classified frontier cyber capability benchmark with voluntary up-to-30-day pre-release government access for covered frontier models, while explicitly rejecting mandatory model licensing.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: EO 14409 is dominantly framed around national_security, centering on new national-security considerations from advanced AI cyber capabilities, protecting American intellectual property from adversaries, defending National Security Systems and Department of War IT, and running an NSA-led classified frontier cyber benchmark. National_security edges out innovation_enablement because nearly every operative section deploys defense, intelligence, and homeland-security authorities to harden systems and confront external threats. Innovation_enablement is a prominent secondary frame—rejecting burdensome regulation and mandatory licensing in favor of voluntary industry collaboration and early trusted-partner access—supported by economic_competitiveness (global AI dominance and investment) and consumer_public_safety (defending rural hospitals, community banks, local utilities, and prosecuting cybercrime).

evidence_spans.quote: Advanced AI capabilities make our Nation stronger, but also introduce new national security considerations that require coordinated action across executive departments and agencies (agencies), and components.
We will continue to lead an America First cybersecurity effort that enhances both our national security and our global AI dominance.

The United States continues to lead the world in Artificial Intelligence (AI) because of the enormous talent and innovation of our AI industry, and because we refuse to stifle this innovation with overly burdensome regulation.

My Administration has unleashed tremendous technological growth and economic investment in AI by slashing the bureaucratic constraints that the prior administration placed on America's AI developers and researchers, and by instead encouraging AI innovation and accelerating responsible AI adoption across government and industry.

facilitate access to cybersecurity tools and services including, where appropriate, covered frontier models for agencies, State and local authorities, and operators of critical infrastructure such as rural hospitals, community banks, and local utilities.
